title: Women's History Month: Shaping the next generation - NewsBreak
text:
By Mina Fuqua ,
3 hours ago
LANSING, MI — What started in a Lansing living room with just a handful of children has now grown into a thriving early learning center serving dozens of families across the community.
“I started this business out of my home and out of my living room terrified, but it is the best decision that I’ve ever made,” said Jacqueline Taylor, founder of Little Dreamers.
(WLNS) Since 2015, Taylor has expanded Little Dreamers into a full early learning center focused on providing a safe and supportive environment for children.
“Parents need a healthy, safe, nurturing, warm and loving environment to put their children in,” Taylor said.
But she says this work goes beyond childcare. It is about early development during one of the most critical stages of life.
“80% of brain development is happening between zero to three. There’s no other industry where you can have that type of direct impact,” she said.
Across Mid-Michigan, that type of care is in high demand.
“We’re currently at a four to one ratio, meaning for every four kiddos, there’s only one childcare slot available,” said Emma Bostwick with LEAP.
That gap is why organizations like LEAP are working to support providers. They help them expand, connect with resources, and stay in business.
“It doesn’t work if childcare doesn’t work,” Bostwick said.
Even with that support, providers say funding continues to be one of the biggest challenges.
“Without proper reimbursements, it puts a heavy burden on parents. That is why childcare is so expensive,” Taylor said.
It creates a difficult balance. Providers struggle to pay staff, and families struggle to afford care.
“We’re somewhere in that intersection trying to figure out a solution that is beneficial for everyone,” Taylor said.
Still, inside Little Dreamers, the impact is clear.
“The foundation of literally a human being’s life is being established now,” said Program Director Maria Robertson.
For many families, that support can be life-changing.
“If I didn’t find your location, I would not have returned to work or finished school,” Taylor said, recalling what one parent shared with her.
And for Taylor, the mission is far from over.
“I would love to influence policy so we can continue to pass things that are beneficial for providers, parents, and children,” she said.
Now with plans to expand and influence policy in early childhood education, Taylor says her mission remains the same. It is to create a safe, loving space for children in her community.
